categories.title: Doors and openings
categories.summary: Common door sizes and FPS openings

entries.title: US interior door, 30 in
entries.kindNote: Common US interior door, 80 × 30 in.
entries.tip: FPS doors are often scaled 1.2–1.5× (about 244–305 uu tall) so openings read clearly at speed.

entries.title: US interior door, 32 in
entries.kindNote: Common US interior door, 80 × 32 in.
entries.tip: A 32 in leaf is a frequent bedroom or hall door. Scale it up in an FPS if the silhouette feels tight.

entries.title: US exterior door, 36 in
entries.kindNote: Common US exterior or passage door, 80 × 36 in. ADA clear width of 32 in usually needs this leaf size.
entries.tip: Use this as a real-world front door. In an FPS, a 36 in opening can still feel narrow in first person.

entries.title: Commercial door, 7 ft
entries.kindNote: 84 in height is common on commercial doors. 80 in is still used too.
entries.tip: A slightly taller leaf helps public spaces feel bigger. Pair with a wider opening for two-person traffic.

entries.title: Door thickness
entries.kindNote: Common US slab thicknesses.
entries.tip: 1⅜ in interior, 1¾ in exterior. Keep door meshes close to this unless you want a heavy vault or bunker door.

entries.title: FPS corridor width
entries.kindNote: Level-design convention, not a building measurement.
entries.tip: 120–150 uu feels tight in first person. 200–300 uu is a comfortable combat hall. Add pockets of 100 uu cover.

categories.title: Stairs and ramps
categories.summary: Risers, treads, ramps, and walkable slopes

entries.title: Comfortable stair, 7-11
entries.kindNote: The 7-11 rule of thumb: 7 in riser and 11 in tread, about 32.5°. Not a single legal standard.
entries.tip: A good first setting for walkable stairs in Thespia. Keep flights readable; bare 7-11 can look thin in first person.

entries.title: US residential stair limits
entries.kindNote: International Residential Code figures widely used in the US.
entries.tip: 7¾ in max riser, 10 in min tread, 36 in min width, 6 ft 8 in headroom. Do not exceed these if a space should feel build-code real.

entries.title: ADA ramp
entries.kindNote: ADA maximum slope is 1:12. Max rise per run is 30 in. Min clear width is 36 in.
entries.tip: Use 1:12 for accessible ramps. A walkable combat ramp can be steeper, but stay under the 44.77° engine limit or the character will slide.

entries.title: Typical stair pitch
entries.kindNote: Comfortable stairs usually fall between 30° and 37°.
entries.tip: Above about 37° stairs feel steep. Anything at or over 44.77° is not walkable with default Character Movement.

categories.title: Ceilings and floors
categories.summary: Room height and modular grid sizes

entries.title: US residential ceiling, 8 ft
entries.kindNote: The common finished ceiling height in US houses.
entries.tip: A solid default for interiors. In an FPS, 8 ft can feel low once you add lights, beams, or a taller capsule, so many levels use 270–300 uu.

entries.title: Residential ceiling, 9 ft
entries.kindNote: Common in newer US houses, not a single required standard.
entries.tip: Gives a little more headroom for lights and destruction debris without jumping to a hall or lobby scale.

entries.title: US minimum habitable ceiling
entries.kindNote: US IRC minimum for habitable rooms is 7 ft. Some exceptions exist for beams and sloped ceilings.
entries.tip: Use 7 ft for basements, bunkers, or tight safe rooms. It will feel cramped in first person, which can be the point.

entries.title: Base-building grid module
entries.kindNote: A common RTS and foundation increment, not a real-world measurement.
entries.tip: 1 m or 2 m cells snap walls, foundations, and fences cleanly in uu. Pick one grid and keep door openings on that module.

entries.title: Default crouched capsule
entries.kindNote: ACharacter CrouchedHalfHeight is 40 uu in UE 5.6, so the crouched capsule is 80 cm tall.
entries.tip: Cover has to be taller than 80 uu to hide a default crouched character. 90–100 uu is the usual starting point.

entries.title: Crouch cover
entries.kindNote: Level-design convention, just above the default 80 cm crouched capsule.
entries.tip: About 100 uu hides a default crouch and still lets the pose read as cover, not a full wall.

entries.title: Half cover / fire-over
entries.kindNote: Level-design convention for waist-to-chest cover you can shoot over.
entries.tip: 100–110 uu is a common fire-over height for crates, low walls, and windowsills in an FPS.

entries.title: Standing / full cover
entries.kindNote: Level-design convention. Default standing capsule is 176 cm; Manny is treated as 180 cm.
entries.tip: 180 uu hides Manny tightly. 200 uu is safer once you add hats, gun raise, or a slightly taller hero capsule.

entries.title: Default max step height
entries.kindNote: UCharacterMovementComponent MaxStepHeight is 45 uu in UE 5.6.
entries.tip: The default character walks onto ledges up to 45 uu. Anything taller needs a jump, vault, or a lower lip.

entries.title: Kitchen counter
entries.kindNote: Standard US kitchen counter height is 36 in.
entries.tip: A good worktop and a high half-cover line. In first person it sits just under a comfortable fire-over.

entries.title: Dining table
entries.kindNote: Most dining tables are 28–30 in. 30 in is the usual setting.
entries.tip: Use 30 in for kitchen and dining tables. It reads as furniture, not cover, unless you flip it.

entries.title: Desk
entries.kindNote: Common desk height is 29–30 in. 29 in is a frequent office setting.
entries.tip: Keep office desks near 29 in so chairs and monitors still fit a 176–180 cm character.

entries.title: Bar counter
entries.kindNote: Standard US bar height is 42 in.
entries.tip: 42 in is a standing drink rail and a solid fire-over. It is just above typical half cover.

entries.title: Bathroom vanity
entries.kindNote: Traditional US vanities are often 32 in. Comfort-height vanities are 34–36 in.
entries.tip: Use 32 in for older baths and 36 in if the vanity should line up with a kitchen counter.

entries.title: Typical midsize sedan
entries.kindNote: Approximate current midsize sedan range, not one model.
entries.tip: Leave extra width for mirrors (often near 2.0 m overall) and a little length if the car must turn in an alley.

entries.title: Typical midsize SUV
entries.kindNote: Approximate current midsize SUV range, not one model.
entries.tip: SUV height is close to Manny's eye line. A standing character barely sees over the roof.

entries.title: Typical full-size pickup
entries.kindNote: Crew-cab full-size trucks vary a lot with bed length. These figures are a typical range.
entries.tip: Plan gates and parking for the long end of this range. The cab roof is full standing cover.

entries.title: US parking stall
entries.kindNote: 9 × 18 ft is a common US planning stall. Some lots use 8.5 × 18 ft.
entries.tip: A reliable stall for base courtyards and lots. Tighten only if you want a cramped, urban feel.

entries.title: US highway lane
entries.kindNote: 12 ft is the common US highway lane width (AASHTO). Urban lanes are often 10–11 ft.
entries.tip: Use 12 ft for roads that should feel like a highway. 10 ft is tighter and reads as a city street.

entries.title: Residential privacy fence
entries.kindNote: 6 ft is the common US backyard privacy fence height.
entries.tip: Just taller than Manny, so it works as standing cover. A 6 ft fence with no gap will fully hide a default capsule.

entries.title: Picket or yard fence
entries.kindNote: Decorative and front-yard fences are commonly about 4 ft.
entries.tip: 4 ft is high half-cover: you can see over it standing, and it hides a crouch if the boards are solid.

entries.title: Residential guard height
entries.kindNote: US IRC residential guards are typically 36 in minimum on open sides more than 30 in above the floor.
entries.tip: Use 36 in on house stairs, landings, and decks. It lines up with a kitchen counter.

entries.title: Commercial guard height
entries.kindNote: US commercial / IBC guards are typically 42 in minimum.
entries.tip: Use 42 in on public stairs, balconies, and catwalks. It matches a bar-counter fire-over line.

entries.title: Interior wall thickness
entries.kindNote: US wood-stud walls with 1/2 in drywall on both sides: 2×4 is 4.5 in, 2×6 is 6.5 in.
entries.tip: Keep ordinary interior walls near 4.5 in. Thicker 2×6 walls suit exteriors or services. Exaggerated walls are fine if they need to read as cover.

entries.title: Default character capsule
entries.kindNote: ACharacter default in UE 5.6: capsule half-height 88, radius 34. Same values as earlier UE5 releases.
entries.tip: The official pawn size is 176 cm tall and 68 cm wide. Build doorways and cover against this capsule, not just the mesh.

entries.title: UE5 Manny height
entries.kindNote: Manny is built for the 176 cm default capsule. This app treats standing height as 180 cm (about 5 ft 11 in). Exact mesh height varies slightly with pose and hair.
entries.tip: The converter's “percent of Manny” uses 180 cm. If your hero uses a custom capsule, measure against that instead.

entries.title: Default eye height
entries.kindNote: APawn BaseEyeHeight is 64 uu above the capsule center. With a 88 uu half-height, the camera sits 152 cm off the ground.
entries.tip: 152 uu is the default first-person or follow-camera eye line. Window sills and cover should be judged from here, not from the top of the head.

entries.title: Default crouch pose
entries.kindNote: CrouchedHalfHeight is 40 uu. CrouchedEyeHeight is 32 uu above the crouched capsule center, so the eye line is 72 cm off the ground.
entries.tip: Default crouch is very low. If a 72 uu eye line feels too sunk, raise CrouchedHalfHeight and the cover heights together.

entries.title: Default max step height
entries.kindNote: UCharacterMovementComponent MaxStepHeight is 45 uu in UE 5.6.
entries.tip: Kerbs, stairs, and rubble under 45 uu can be walked. Taller lips need a ramp, a jump, or a vault ability.

entries.title: Default max walkable slope
entries.kindNote: WalkableFloorAngle defaults to 44.773°. That is acos(0.71), the default WalkableFloorZ.
entries.tip: Ramps at or above 44.77° are not walkable with default movement. Keep combat ramps clearly under this, around 30° or less if they should feel comfortable.

entries.title: Default jump height
entries.kindNote: Derived from default JumpZVelocity 420 and gravity 980: height = 420² / (2 × 980) = 90 cm.
entries.tip: A default jump clears 90 uu. Combined with the 45 uu step, a character can mount ledges a little over 90 uu if the lip is forgiving.

entries.title: Default max walk speed
entries.kindNote: MaxWalkSpeed defaults to 600 uu/s (6 m/s). That is a run, not a casual walk. MaxWalkSpeedCrouched defaults to 300 uu/s.
entries.tip: At 6 m/s, openings and stairs need more clearance than real life. This is one reason FPS doors are often scaled 1.2–1.5×.
